archetypes.name: scope-drift
archetypes.rationale: Plan explicitly forbids modifying python/bootstrap.py, but the diff changes _phase_coder; test-implement-structure.sh and several docs also appear outside the stated /design-only scope.
archetypes.prompt_body: The implementation plan explicitly states 'Do not modify python/bootstrap.py' and limits scope to /design launcher, /design fences, /design references, /design pause/resume CI harness, and /design structure tests. Examine all changed files and flag any that fall outside this boundary: python/bootstrap.py (_phase_coder coder-priority swap from codex-first to cursor-first), scripts/test-implement-structure.sh (stall-recovery needle additions), docs/review-agents.md (round-2+ panel description), and docs/topology.md (panel_slots description change). For each out-of-scope change, determine whether it is load-bearing for this PR's feature or is an independent side-change that should be split out. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: launcher-atomics
archetypes.rationale: The new os.fchmod call in _atomic_write affects all callers, not just the launcher; directory creation in _write_design_run_sh precedes the symlink ancestry check, creating a potential ordering hazard.
archetypes.prompt_body: In python/session_env.py, os.fchmod(fd, mode) was added immediately after os.open() inside _atomic_write. Enumerate every caller of _atomic_write and verify that applying exact mode bits (bypassing umask) is the intended behavior for each, including the 0o600 session-env files. In _write_design_run_sh, run_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) executes before _assert_no_symlink_path_or_ancestors(run_path); assess whether a symlink introduced between these two calls could allow directory creation under a redirected path before the guard fires. In _design_run_launcher_text, the case pattern *..* matches any basename containing consecutive dots (e.g. foo..bar.sh), potentially over-rejecting valid wrapper names; verify this is intentional and consistent with the plan's stated basename validation rules. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
